input: A centrifugal pump is used to move caustic solution between two vessels that stand at grade. The duty point is the flow and head at which the pump is required to run in normal service. The head, it should be explained, is the height of a column of the pumped liquid that the pressure rise at the pump is able to support, stated for the liquid being pumped; with the two vessels standing at grade, the head is not spent on a large static lift between them. Taken together, the figures that follow describe the pump at the one operating point that the process asks of it. At the duty point, the flow is 44 m3 h-1 against a head of 51 m, and the pump efficiency is 81%. The shaft power at the duty point is 7.5 kW; it should be understood that the shaft power is the hydraulic power imparted to the liquid divided by the pump efficiency, so the efficiency is already contained within the stated figure and must not be applied a second time. The motor is rated 15% above the shaft power, which corresponds to a rated output of 8.6 kW, and this margin is intended to cover motor loading at the duty point with headroom for the fall in efficiency and the rise in absorbed power that wear and off-duty operation can bring. The shaft power is the power that the motor must deliver to the pump shaft at that particular duty, after the pump's own inefficiency has taken its share of the power imparted to the liquid. Cavitation was not observed during the acceptance test. However, the acceptance test ran for 4 h at the duty point only. The absence of cavitation is therefore established at the duty point over a run of that length; cavitation at flows away from the duty point, at lower suction levels or at other liquid temperatures was not tested, and the test makes no statement whatsoever about them.

At the duty point the flow is 44 m3 h-1 against a head of 51 m, and the pump efficiency is 81%. The shaft power at the duty point is 7.5 kW; the shaft power is the hydraulic power imparted to the liquid divided by the pump efficiency, so the efficiency is already inside the stated figure and is not to be applied a second time. The motor is rated 15% above the shaft power, a rated output of 8.6 kW, and the margin covers motor loading at the duty point with headroom for the fall in efficiency and the rise in absorbed power that wear and off-duty operation bring. Shaft power is the power the motor must deliver to the pump shaft at that duty, after the pump's own inefficiency has taken its share of the power imparted to the liquid. Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test. The acceptance test ran for 4 h at the duty point only. Absence of cavitation is therefore established at the duty point over a run of that length; cavitation at flows away from the duty point, at lower suction levels or at other liquid temperatures was not tested, and the test makes no statement about them.
